$schema_note: Shared test vectors for the three-way plan-status classifier. AUTHORED in qontinui-dev-notes; VENDORED into qontinui-web. Two repos cannot share a file (no package dependency, and no qontinui-dev-notes workflow checks out a sibling repo), so the copy is made DETECTABLE instead: both repos pin this file's content_sha256 in a constant (plan_status_classifier.VECTORS_SHA256 here) and each suite asserts the file it holds hashes to it. A divergence reds both suites on the next run. (D7)

measured_against.note: Corpus counts drift hourly; the LIVE fixtures below are pinned observations, not current state.

cascade_order_note: FIRST-MATCH-WINS. The order is part of the spec (D6), not an implementation detail: several members match one row at once, and without a stated order the two implementations pick different winners on the same input. Vectors tagged `asserts_order` exist only to pin a specific precedence. NOTE on arm 6: NO_CITATIONS_CAPTURED requires a terminality claim on some axis in ADDITION to evidence_complete:true and zero citations. Without that third condition it also swallows every genuinely-unstarted plan (measured 235 of its 351 rows on 2026-09-03) and AGREE_OPEN becomes unreachable; see `regression/both-open-zero-citations-must-be-AGREE_OPEN`.

vectors.name: live/2026-05-17-runner-auto-login-initial-mount
vectors.why: The plan's headline row. coord stored status `shipped`, document stamp `draft` on origin/main, and the LIVE delivery predicate reads shipped:false with evidence_complete:false. Arm 5 must win over arm 7 and arm 10: under an incomplete evidence read, shipped:false is not an observation.

evidence_gaps: qontinui/qontinui-runner#164 reads unmerged on a STALE cached row that could not be re-read live — cannot tell "not landed" from "we did not look"

expect_reason_contains: qontinui/qontinui-runner#164 reads unmerged on a STALE cached row that could not be re-read live — cannot tell "not landed" from "we did not look"

vectors.name: live/2026-09-03-stacked-prs-citation-convention-generates-endless-correction-prs
vectors.why: coord accepted status:'' silently (Free transition tier). It is not null and not a vocabulary word, so it detaches the unit from every status query. 410 units held this value on 2026-09-03.

vectors.name: live/2026-06-18-coord-merge-scheduler-db-test-harness
vectors.why: Direction (d)'s row AS MEASURED: coord status '', document stamp `shipped`, zero citations, delivery {shipped:false, evidence_complete:true, gaps:[]}. The empty stored status is read FIRST, which is itself the ordering claim.

vectors.name: live/2026-06-18-coord-merge-scheduler-db-test-harness+nonempty-unit-status
vectors.why: The same live row with ONLY the empty stored status replaced by `draft`, so the cascade reaches direction (d) itself: the DOCUMENT stamp claims `shipped` while coord looked and found nothing, and 'found nothing' is rendered identically to 'nothing to find' everywhere else. The terminality claim here comes from axis B, not axis A.

vectors.name: live/2026-06-16-wire-agent-durability-daemons
vectors.why: The A-vs-C class, live: coord's STORED column says `in_progress` while coord's own LIVE delivery predicate says shipped:true over a complete read of 3 citations. The stored column and the derived verdict are two different facts and they disagree -- which is why axis A is retained rather than collapsed into axis C. Measured 2026-09-03.

vectors.name: live/2026-06-13-coord-tier2-specialist-auto-invocation
vectors.why: A stamp a human reads and the adapter does not. The linter's looser grammar parses `in progress` and calls it `ok`; no line in the body satisfies the byte-exact `> **Status:` test, so the adapter substitutes `draft`. Measured 2026-09-03; 60 rows carried this class that day.

vectors.name: live/2026-05-17-sdk-canonical-shape-unification
vectors.why: DOC_UNDERSTATES, live: coord derived `shipped` from 2 merged citations and the body on origin/main still reads `in progress`. This is the population qontinui-dev-notes#445 already repairs -- the correction goes to the BODY, never to coord, because `shipped` is derived and a direct write is 422 status_is_derived. Measured 2026-09-03.

vectors.name: live/2026-06-07-ui-bridge-friction-action-params-and-exited-tombstones
vectors.why: What full agreement actually looks like on this corpus: stored status `shipped`, body stamped `shipped` and adapter-readable, and a complete delivery read over 2 citations. 249 of 1558 stems reached this class on 2026-09-03. Measured live.

vectors.name: axis-unreadable/coord-transport-dead
vectors.why: The plan's central claim in vector form: with no coord transport, axes A and C are UNREADABLE and the row must NOT fall through into agreement.

vectors.name: axis-unreadable/linter-unresolvable
vectors.why: lint-plan-status.py could not be resolved. Axis B is UNKNOWN naming axis B -- there is deliberately no home-grown fallback parse (D2).

vectors.name: axis-unreadable/citation-read-failed-for-one-slug
vectors.why: A per-slug citation read failed while the rest of the corpus read fine. Only axis C is named, and only this row degrades.

vectors.name: no-body/coord-unit-with-no-plan-on-main
vectors.why: 73 units on 2026-09-03 had no top-level plans/*.md on origin/main. The document axis has no value, so the row is UNKNOWN rather than compared against a default.

vectors.name: no-body/both-sides-absent-body-wins
vectors.why: Both joined sides absent. Arm 2 precedes arm 3, so the answer is deterministic rather than whichever check an implementation happened to write first.

vectors.name: no-unit/plan-on-main-with-no-coord-unit
vectors.why: 139 bodies on 2026-09-03 had no coord work unit. Axes A and C have no value.

vectors.name: empty-unit-status/precedes-evidence-incomplete
vectors.why: A unit with status '' whose delivery ALSO reads evidence_complete:false satisfies two members at once. D6's whole reason for existing: arm 4 wins.

vectors.name: empty-unit-status/whitespace-only
vectors.why: A status of whitespace is the empty string for every practical purpose and must not be read as an off-vocabulary word.

vectors.name: evidence-incomplete/gaps-carried-verbatim
vectors.why: evidence_gaps must be carried VERBATIM into the reason, never collapsed or summarised: the gap text is the only thing that says WHICH of coord's three modelled degradations fired.

vectors.name: evidence-incomplete/precedes-doc-overstates
vectors.why: Doc terminal, unit open -- which would be DOC_OVERSTATES -- but the evidence read is incomplete, so arm 5 wins and the doc comparison is not reported as established.

vectors.name: no-citations/precedes-unit-status-contradicts-delivery
vectors.why: status `shipped` over a COMPLETE evidence read of zero citations -- both axes claim the work landed. Both arm 6 and arm 7 match; arm 6 wins, because 'coord captured nothing while something claims it is done' is the more specific fact.

vectors.name: contradiction/unit-says-shipped-delivery-says-not
vectors.why: The A-vs-C class in its plainest form, over a COMPLETE evidence read with citations actually captured -- so shipped:false IS an observation here.

vectors.name: contradiction/delivery-says-shipped-unit-is-open
vectors.why: The other direction: the live predicate says shipped, the stored column says `draft`. On this tenant the derive worker runs mode=live but coord's own health verdict for it reads `dead`, so the stored column is INTERMITTENTLY correct -- exactly what a per-row class surfaces and an aggregate cannot.

vectors.name: contradiction/abandoned-unit-with-shipped-delivery
vectors.why: `superseded` is terminal but not shipped-class, so it does not trip the first arm; a delivery verdict of shipped:true over it still is a genuine disagreement.

vectors.name: contradiction/off-vocabulary-unit-status-done
vectors.why: `done` is outside EVERY documented vocabulary and coord stores it anyway (8 units on 2026-09-03). It reads shipped-class here, so a shipped:false delivery contradicts it.

vectors.name: doc-unreadable/underscore-form-the-linter-calls-ok
vectors.why: THE VOCABULARY TRAP. lint-plan-status.py's ADAPTER_VOCAB carries eleven spellings and classifies `in_progress` as `ok`; the Rust adapter tokenizes NINE phrases with a starts_with + word-boundary test, and 'in_progress'.starts_with('in progress') is false. So this stamp is genuinely unreadable by the adapter.

vectors.name: doc-unreadable/no-status-block-at-all
vectors.why: 45 bodies on origin/main carried no status block at all (linter totals, f105b111). The adapter silently defaults them to `draft` and can push that over a status coord had derived -- so this is never rendered as an open document.

vectors.name: doc-unreadable/human-readable-but-not-byte-exact
vectors.why: The linter's looser grammar accepts an unquoted, unbolded stamp; the adapter's byte-exact `> **Status:` test does not. A human and the adapter read different statuses off the same body, which is the gap D2 refuses to reconcile away.

vectors.name: doc-unreadable/off-vocabulary-word
vectors.why: 115 bodies carried an off-vocabulary word on f105b111 (`complete`, `landed`, `proposed`, `planned`...). The adapter keeps it verbatim rather than tokenizing it.

vectors.name: doc-unreadable/precedes-doc-overstates
vectors.why: Doc terminal, unit open -- DOC_OVERSTATES on terminality alone -- but the stamp is not adapter-readable, so the comparison rests on a value the adapter never sees. Arm 8 wins.

vectors.name: doc-overstates/doc-shipped-unit-in-progress
vectors.why: 67 rows on the plan's first measurement. The body says the work landed; coord's unit does not.

vectors.name: doc-understates/unit-shipped-doc-draft
vectors.why: 169 rows on the plan's first measurement, and the population qontinui-dev-notes#445 already repairs. This surface hands it over; it does not re-repair, and it never hand-writes `shipped`.

vectors.name: agree-terminal/both-shipped
vectors.why: Every axis was READ and both terminality readings agree. Reachable only because arm 1 already proved no axis was missing.

vectors.name: agree-terminal/both-superseded
vectors.why: Abandonment agrees too: `superseded` is terminal on both axes, and coord's delivery reads shipped:false over a complete evidence read -- which is not a contradiction, because a superseded unit never claimed to have landed.

vectors.name: agree-open/both-draft
vectors.why: The plainest agreement, and still only reachable at the END of the cascade.

vectors.name: agree-open/vetted-vs-in-progress-both-open
vectors.why: Different words, same terminality reading. The classifier compares terminality, not string equality -- coord's stored vocabulary and the document's are not the same set.

vectors.name: agree-open/off-vocabulary-unit-status-reads-open
vectors.why: `ready` and `proposed` are stored on this tenant and are in no terminal set, so they read OPEN. That reading is stated here rather than assumed, because axis A is not drawn from a closed set.

vectors.name: regression/both-open-zero-citations-must-be-AGREE_OPEN
vectors.why: REGRESSION GUARD for the arm-6 tightening. `NO_CITATIONS_CAPTURED` requires a THIRD condition beyond evidence_complete:true and zero citations -- at least one axis must actually CLAIM the work is done. Here both axes are open and there are no citations, because the plan has not started; coord captured nothing for the ordinary reason. Without the third condition this row lands in arm 6, which sits above the agreement arms -- and the first live corpus run measured that cost: 351 rows in arm 6 of which 235 were this exact shape, driving AGREE_OPEN to ZERO over a corpus that is mostly open. If this vector ever reports NO_CITATIONS_CAPTURED, the predicate was loosened back and the classifier can no longer observe agreement-on-open.
vectors.asserts_order: NO_CITATIONS_CAPTURED requires a terminality claim, so this falls through to AGREE_OPEN

vectors.name: regression/both-open-zero-citations-in-progress-and-vetted
vectors.why: The same guard over the two commonest OPEN words on this corpus (`in_progress` 104 and `draft` 80 of the 235 measured). Different words, same terminality reading, still agreement rather than a manufactured finding.
